Let's use our newly-acquired knoweledge to gain a bit of insight onto the carreer of Serena Williams. 

First, let's attach the package we need: 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
```

Second, let's import and wrangle the data: execute the following chunk:

```{r}
wta_data <-
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gruggeri/tennis_wta/master/wta_grand_slam_data.csv" %>% 
  read_csv(col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
```

- Now, let's use a `{dplyr}` verb to pick the columns  variables `year`, `match_num`, `winner_name`,`loser_name`, `tourney_name`,`round`. Inspect some of the values in these columns. Can you find an interpretation? 

- What type is the columns `year` and `match_num`? Use a `{dplyr}` verb to transform them into `numeric`. 

- Use a `{dplyr}` verb to subset the dataset to the matches played (won or lost) by Serena. 

- Use one of the `{dplyr}` verbs to sort these matches chronologically! Think of the column(s) that you'll use.

- Subset the data again to find the number of times Serena got to the final round of the tournament!

```{r}
wta_data %>% 
  select(year, match_num, winner_name,loser_name, tourney_name,round) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year), 
         match_num = as.numeric(match_num)) %>% 
  filter(winner_name == "Serena Williams" | loser_name == "Serena Williams") %>% 
  arrange(year, tourney_name, match_num) %>% 
  filter(round=="F")
```
